about.title: About Cash Out Refinance Calculator - Home Equity Access Tool
about.description: The Cash Out Refinance Calculator is a refinancing planning tool designed to help homeowners estimate the costs and tradeoffs of cash-out refinancing. This calculator helps you review how much cash you may be able to access from your home equity, new monthly payments, and how a cash-out refinance compares with other borrowing options. Whether you're consolidating debt, funding home improvements, or covering other expenses, this tool provides scenario-based estimates for cash-out refinance planning.

howTo.title: How to Use the Cash Out Refinance Calculator

steps.title: Enter Current Mortgage Details
steps.description: Input your current mortgage balance, interest rate, and remaining loan term.

steps.title: Set Home Value
steps.description: Enter your current home value based on recent appraisal or market analysis.

steps.description: Enter how much cash you want to take out from your home equity.

steps.title: Enter New Loan Terms
steps.description: Input the new interest rate and loan term for the cash-out refinance.

steps.title: Add Closing Costs
steps.description: Include estimated closing costs and fees for the refinancing transaction.

steps.title: Compare Scenarios
steps.description: Review payment changes, cash received, and break-even analysis.

faq.q: How much cash can I get from a cash-out refinance?
faq.a: Most lenders allow cash-out refinancing up to 80% of your home's value. For example, if your home is worth $400,000 and you owe $200,000, you could potentially access up to $120,000 cash ($400,000 × 80% - $200,000 = $120,000).

faq.q: When might cash-out refinancing be worth considering?
faq.a: Cash-out refinancing may be worth considering when you can lower your rate, need funds for a specific purpose, or want to compare it against higher-rate debt. Review closing costs, your new loan balance, and the long-term payment impact before deciding.

faq.q: What are the risks of cash-out refinancing?
faq.a: Risks include increasing your mortgage balance, extending your loan term, potential for higher payments, and reduced home equity. You're also converting home equity (illiquid) into cash, which might be spent rather than invested wisely.

faq.q: How do cash-out refinance rates compare to regular refinance rates?
faq.a: Cash-out refinance rates are typically 0.125% to 0.25% higher than rate-and-term refinance rates. They are often lower than credit card rates, personal loans, or some HELOC offers, so they can be useful to compare when reviewing borrowing options.
